title: Document checklist positions and structured argument schemas in command help
summary: Document checklist positions and structured argument schemas in command help
description:
Reported from the cli-test review and Orbitfall project exercise on 2026-09-04. Installed tools: Lore 0.4.1 and Quest 0.3.2, macOS ARM64. Source review revisions: Lore 054e6590f1b81fda418c9891611f84fd35aacf6e; Quest dcb06f6520e08f2755c04166cca168318a94ae5a. Findings describe those tested versions, not a claim that current HEAD was retested. Evidence paths below are retained in the sibling cli-test checkout; the reproduction and outcomes are also included here. Filing is not a fix.

Orbitfall exercised task/draft creation, promotion, checklist updates and lifecycle operations with Quest 0.3.2. Create a task with explicit actor flags and --acceptance-criteria '["First","Second"]', then view it as JSON: acceptanceCriteria entries expose index 0 and 1. Passing --check-ac 0 to task edit exits 2: "--check-ac must be a 1-based positive integer." Passing listed position 1 works.
The semantics are implemented (QCLI-138 and QCLI-146, both Done), but quest help task edit --json lists flag names without the input grammar or explaining that CLI positions differ from JSON index metadata. The same discoverability gap affects JSON-array checklist inputs and structured comment objects; natural-text guesses produced usage errors during the exercise.
Scope: improve executable help/examples/schema discovery, preserve the existing positional semantics. Explain what happens after checklist removal so agents do not persist stale positions. Include structured comments and edit-batch examples rather than requiring callers to infer object shapes from errors.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Help explicitly distinguishes 1-based CLI checklist positions from returned JSON index metadata for check/uncheck/remove AC and DoD.
Executable examples show task creation, checking/removing an item, rereading and addressing the remaining checklist.
Help or linked machine-readable schemas specify valid checklist arrays, structured comment objects and edit-batch records, with examples verified against the CLI.

plan: Expand command-help.ts's "task edit" summary: explicitly distinguish 1-based CLI checklist positions (--check-ac/--uncheck-ac/--remove-ac and the DoD equivalents) from the JSON envelope's 0-based index field, explain that removal renumbers remaining items (positions and indices both), and document --comments/--add-comment's required {id,authorId,body,createdAt} JSON array shape.
Expand task edit-batch's summary with a concrete JSONL operation-record example ({reference, operationId, patch}).

Add an executable checklist recipe to the task-creation guide: create a task with two acceptance criteria, check position 1, remove position 1, reread, then address the item that renumbered into position 1 -- demonstrating the exact stale-position pitfall the report described, using a fresh task rather than the shared T-1 record other guide recipes depend on.

Add a dedicated test that runs the --comments/--add-comment JSON example and an edit-batch JSONL example for real against a test store, so the documented shapes are verified against the CLI, not just asserted in prose.
Update guide-commands.test.ts's exact recipe count and placeholder map for the new task-creation recipes.
implementationNotes: AC1: expanded command-help.ts's 'task edit' summary to explicitly distinguish 1-based CLI checklist positions (--check-ac/--uncheck-ac/--remove-ac and the --*-dod equivalents) from the JSON envelope's 0-based index field (position N = index N-1), and to explain that removal renumbers everything after it in both forms. AC2: added a 'Checklist positions renumber after a removal' section to the task-creation guide with an executable recipe (create with two ACs, check position 1, remove position 1, reread via task view, then check position 1 again -- now addressing what was originally the second item) demonstrating exactly the stale-position pitfall from the report; runs against a fresh task rather than the shared T-1 record other guide recipes depend on, verified by guide-commands.test.ts's real execution (not just prose). AC3: documented --comments/--add-comment's required {id,authorId,body,createdAt} JSON array shape in 'task edit', and task edit-batch's {reference,operationId,patch} JSONL record shape with a patch-field example; added a new test/contract/command-help-examples.test.ts that runs the literal documented shapes against a real store for both, so the shapes are verified against the CLI rather than only asserted in prose.
finalSummary: The semantics were already correct (QCLI-138/QCLI-146); this closed the discoverability gap Orbitfall hit: quest help task edit --json listed flag names with no grammar. Fixed with docs only, no behavior change: (1) task edit's help summary now explains 1-based CLI checklist positions vs the JSON envelope's 0-based index, and that removal renumbers everything after it; (2) a new task-creation guide section shows this as an executable recipe (create, check, remove, reread, address the renumbered item) against a fresh task, so it never touches the shared T-1 record other guide recipes depend on; (3) --comments/--add-comment's {id,authorId,body,createdAt} shape and edit-batch's {reference,operationId,patch} JSONL shape are now documented in help text, with a new dedicated test running both literal shapes against a real store so the docs can't silently drift from what the CLI actually accepts. bun run check: 430/430 tests green.
